D16's full brightness at 16 internal pixels. C10's `### Draw descriptors and motion keys (...)` subsection stays where
it is. It takes no Contents entry, because the Contents list holds only `##` headings:

````markdown
### Temporal anti-aliasing and upscaling (`AntiAliasing.Temporal`)

`Post.Quality.AntiAliasing = AntiAliasing.Temporal` renders the scene at an internal resolution at or below the
window, moves each frame by a sub-pixel jitter, and rebuilds a stable image at the window's full resolution from the
jittered frames and their history. Thin and moving detail such as distant grass holds still while the camera moves,
edges are anti-aliased without MSAA's per-sample cost, and fewer pixels are shaded. It is single-sample: it never
combines with MSAA, and `Pixelated` refuses it.

~~~csharp
scene.Post.Quality.AntiAliasing = AntiAliasing.Temporal;
scene.Post.Temporal.Upscale = TemporalUpscale.Quality;   // Native, Quality, Balanced, Performance or UltraPerformance
scene.Post.Temporal.Sharpness = 0.25f;                   // 0 turns the sharpen off

// A moving body keeps one key for its lifetime. Parts of one body derive theirs.
MotionKey body = MotionKey.From(entityId);
scene.Draw(new RigidInstanceDraw(weapon, weaponWorld) { Motion = MotionKey.Combine(body, 1) });
scene.DrawSkinned(new SkinnedInstanceDraw(bodyMesh, bodyModel) { Motion = body }, bones);

// A teleport, a loading screen or a cutscene cut.
scene.CameraCut();

// The automatic cut, defaults 16 m and 60 degrees.
scene.Post.Temporal.CutDistanceMetres = 24f;
scene.Post.Temporal.CutAngleDegrees = 45f;
~~~

- **Presets.** `Post.Temporal.Upscale` sizes the internal target per axis against the window: `Native` 1.0,
  `Quality` 1/1.5 (44% of the pixels), `Balanced` 1/1.7 (35%), `Performance` 1/2 (25%) and `UltraPerformance` 1/3
  (11%). `UltraPerformance` is for very dense displays: at 3456x2234 it renders 1152x745, fewer pixels than a fixed
  1600x900 target, and its jitter cycle is 72 frames. `Post.Temporal.UpscaleRatio` (0.33 to 1.0) overrides the
  preset. `MaxRenderWidth` and `MaxRenderHeight` still cap the target. While temporal anti-aliasing is on it sizes the
  target itself, the way SSAA forces `MatchViewport`.
- **Sharpening.** A robust contrast adaptive sharpen runs after the tonemap at display resolution.
  `Post.Temporal.Sharpness` runs from 0 (the pass does not run) to 1, default 0.25. It limits each pixel by its four
  neighbours, so it leaves an edge already at full contrast alone and sharpens an isolated pixel at most half as
  hard, which keeps it from bringing back shimmer.
- **Texture detail.** Material textures on models, foliage, splat terrain and tile ground take a mip bias of
  log2(internal / display) plus `Post.Temporal.MipBiasOffset` (default minus 0.5, clamped to minus 2 to plus 1), so
  upscaling does not blur them. Textured billboards and particle atlases are not biased. The bias is exactly zero
  with temporal anti-aliasing off.
- **Keys.** A draw without a `MotionKey` is treated as static and gets camera-only motion, which is right for
  terrain, tile ground and placed props. Give every draw that moves a key: `RigidInstanceDraw.Motion` and
  `SkinnedInstanceDraw.Motion`. A key submitted twice in one frame counts in
  `LastTemporalDiagnostics.KeyCollisions`. A mover without a key reads softer rather than smeared, and the
  `MotionVectors` debug view shows it painted with the camera's motion. `CharacterAvatar`, `Scene3DBinder` and
  `SkinnedLimb` key themselves.
- **Cuts.** History resets on `scene.CameraCut()`, on a window or render scale change, a preset or ratio change, an
  anti-aliasing mode change, a device reset, and automatically when the camera moves further than
  `Post.Temporal.CutDistanceMetres` (16) or turns more than `Post.Temporal.CutAngleDegrees` (60) in one frame. Call
  `CameraCut()` on any jump the camera makes on purpose, so a teleport under 16 m does not blend the old view into the
  new one for a frame. The frame after a reset renders exactly like a fresh scene's first frame.
- **Transparent content.** Particles, billboards, beams, trails, decals and water draw no motion. The resolve lowers
  the history weight wherever they changed the opaque image, so a smoke puff or a splash leaves no trail.
- **Background.** The sky reprojects by the camera's rotation, so its sun stays put in the world while the camera
  turns. The starfield is fixed to the screen, so it takes zero motion and its stars hold still under a turning
  camera. Under temporal anti-aliasing the background draws before the transparent passes, so a beam or billboard
  over the sky shows.
- **Edge outline.** With `Post.Outline` on, temporal anti-aliasing runs the outline on the internal image before the
  resolve, so its lines are accumulated and steady like the rest of the image rather than moving with the jitter.
  With HDR on, the outline colour then passes through the tonemap. Every other mode runs it in the post chain as
  before.
- **Debug views.** `scene.DebugView = SceneDebugView.MotionVectors` works under any mode and shows the motion target,
  hue for direction, brightness for length (full at 16 internal pixels) and black where nothing opaque drew or
  nothing moved. `History` (black fresh, white full history, green where thin
  feature retention holds a pixel), `Disocclusion` (red where history was rejected) and `Reactive` (yellow where
  transparent content lowered the history weight) show the resolve's own decisions and take effect only under
  `AntiAliasing.Temporal`.
- **Diagnostics.** `scene.LastTemporalDiagnostics` reports the frame index, the jitter phase and offset, keyed rigid
  and skinned draws, key collisions, whether history was valid and the last reset reason, the internal and display
  sizes, the preset and the effective `UpscaleRatio`. `scene.RequestTemporalCounts()` samples disoccluded, reactive
  and clipped pixel counts on a 32 by 18 grid on the next frame, and they appear at the following `PrepareFrame`
  with `CountsFrameIndex` naming the frame. Reading them back drains the device once on Metal and Vulkan, so
  request them from a debug overlay a few times a second at most, never every frame. Read the diagnostics on the
  render thread after the frame renders. A second render inside the same frame, such as an offscreen capture,
  leaves them and the history untouched.
- **Cost.** The resolve and the sharpen together measured under 1.0 ms at a 2560x1440 display on Apple silicon
  (`TemporalResolveCostPerfGpuTests`). With temporal anti-aliasing off, nothing of it exists and every frame renders
  byte-identically to before.
````

```markdown
  `.Temporal` renders at a `Post.Temporal.Upscale` preset below the window, jitters each frame and resolves a stable
  full-resolution image from history, with a light RCAS sharpen (`Post.Temporal.Sharpness`) and a material mip bias
  (`Post.Temporal.MipBiasOffset`). Moving draws pass a `MotionKey` through `RigidInstanceDraw` or
  `SkinnedInstanceDraw`, camera jumps call `Scene3D.CameraCut()`, and `Scene3D.DebugView` and
  `LastTemporalDiagnostics` show what the resolve did. See the consumer contract's temporal section.
```

`docs/CROSS-PLATFORM.md`, two bullets after `- **Sampling textures in binding order is retired.**`:

```markdown
- **A texture LOD bias that must hold on every backend is a shader argument, never sampler state.** Metal samplers
  carry no LOD bias, so a sampler's `mipLodBias` applies on Direct3D 11 and Vulkan and is dropped on Metal
  (`SamplerLodBiasGpuTests`). `texture(s, uv, bias)` cross-compiles to an MSL `bias()` argument, to HLSL
  `SampleBias` and to the SPIR-V `Bias` operand, so it holds everywhere. `textureGrad` has no bias argument, so an
  explicit-gradient tap scales both gradients by `exp2(bias)` instead (`ShaderSources.MaterialLodGradGlsl`). A bias
  of exactly 0.0 and a gradient scale of exactly 1.0 leave the tap unchanged on all three backends, which is what
  keeps every golden byte-identical with temporal anti-aliasing off.
- **A read map drains the device on Metal and Vulkan and not on Direct3D 11.** `Map` of a staging resource for
  reading waits for the whole device on Metal and on Vulkan, and only for the mapped resource on Direct3D 11, so no
  readback on the seam is free of a stall on every backend. That is why the temporal counts are sampled on request
  rather than every frame.
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Re-read the version and the tags**

The version is chosen here, at release time, never earlier, by the repository's ride rule. A version `main` has
staged and not yet tagged is ridden when it is a minor, since this program adds public API and a minor can carry it.
A staged patch cannot carry new API, so the program takes the next minor above it and the patch's entry ships inside
this release. A staged version already tagged means nothing is in flight, so the program cuts the next free minor.
`STAGED` is `main`'s `<KhaozEngineVersion>`, `PREVIOUS` is the newest tag (the release the byte-identity sentence
compares against), and `RIDE` says whether the program joins the staged entry or writes its own.

```bash
cd /Users/antonio/KhaozEngine/.worktrees/temporal-foundations
git fetch origin --tags
STAGED=$(git show origin/main:Directory.Build.props | sed -n 's:.*<KhaozEngineVersion>\(.*\)</KhaozEngineVersion>.*:\1:p')
PREVIOUS=$(git tag -l 'v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1 | sed 's/^v//')
IFS=. read -r MAJOR MINOR PATCH <<< "$STAGED"
if git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$STAGED" >/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-remote --tags origin "v$STAGED")" ]; then
  RIDE=no                      # the staged version is released, so nothing is in flight
  MINOR=$((MINOR + 1))
elif [ "$PATCH" = 0 ]; then
  RIDE=yes                     # an untagged staged minor is ridden
else
  RIDE=no                      # an untagged staged patch cannot carry new API
  MINOR=$((MINOR + 1))
fi
if [ "$RIDE" = no ]; then
  while git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$MAJOR.$MINOR.0" >/dev/null; do MINOR=$((MINOR + 1)); done
  V="$MAJOR.$MINOR.0"
else
  V="$STAGED"
fi
echo "main stages $STAGED, newest tag v$PREVIOUS, this release is $V, ride=$RIDE"
git ls-remote --tags origin "v$V"
printf 'V=%s\nSTAGED=%s\nPREVIOUS=%s\nRIDE=%s\n' "$V" "$STAGED" "$PREVIOUS" "$RIDE" > /tmp/taa-release.env
```

Expected: one `echo` line, and `git ls-remote` prints nothing, so `v$V` is free on origin too. At planning time `main`
stages an untagged `20.6.0` (the journal reset, #1150) over the newest tag `v20.5.1`, so the program rides it and this
release is `20.6.0`, unless that session tags it first, in which case the release is `20.7.0`. When `RIDE` is `no`,
set `<KhaozEngineVersion>` in `Directory.Build.props` to `V` in Step 4's commit. Group I pins `V` (Task I1 sets its own
`V` to it).

The steps below write `$V`, `$STAGED` and `$PREVIOUS` in shell and `<V>`, `<STAGED>` and `<PREVIOUS>` in Markdown.
Substitute the chosen values in the Markdown. Shell variables do not survive between steps, so every later block
that reads them starts by sourcing `/tmp/taa-release.env`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the CHANGELOG entry**

When `RIDE` is `yes`, add the paragraphs below under the existing `## <V>` entry, after its current paragraphs, and
drop the `## <V>` heading line from the block. When `RIDE` is `no`, add them as a new top entry above `main`'s staged
`## <STAGED>` entry. Either way write them in the file's voice, with the measured value from `/tmp/taa-measured.txt` (Task H2 Step 2) in the cost sentence:

```markdown
## <V>

`AntiAliasing.Temporal` joins Off, FXAA, MSAA and SSAA ([#1149](https://github.com/APKiwiOrg/KhaozEngine/issues/1149)).
It renders the scene at an internal resolution chosen as a fraction of the window, jitters each frame, and resolves a
stable full-resolution image from the jittered frames and their history: dilated motion, a Catmull-Rom history fetch,
depth disocclusion, Lanczos reconstruction of the jittered samples, variance clipping with thin feature retention and
a reactive estimate for transparent content. Thin and moving detail such as distant grass holds still while the
camera moves. `Post.Temporal.Upscale` picks `Native`, `Quality`, `Balanced`, `Performance` or `UltraPerformance` (1,
1/1.5, 1/1.7, 1/2 and 1/3 per axis), and `Post.Temporal.UpscaleRatio` sets any ratio from 0.33 to 1. `UltraPerformance`
is for very dense displays: at 3456x2234 it shades fewer pixels than a fixed 1600x900 target. A light RCAS sharpen
runs after the tonemap (`Post.Temporal.Sharpness`, default 0.25), and material textures on models, foliage, splat
terrain and tile ground take a mip bias so upscaling does not blur them (`Post.Temporal.MipBiasOffset`, default minus
0.5). The sky reprojects by the camera's rotation, the screen-fixed starfield holds still, and the toon edge outline
runs ahead of the resolve so its lines are steady too. The resolve and the sharpen together measured at most <value>
ms at a 2560x1440 display on Apple silicon, and the motion target added <motion value> ms at 1600x900.

Moving draws report their motion through a caller key. `MotionKey`, and the `RigidInstanceDraw` and
`SkinnedInstanceDraw` descriptors with `Scene3D.Draw(in RigidInstanceDraw)` and
`Scene3D.DrawSkinned(in SkinnedInstanceDraw, ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4>)`, carry it. Every existing `Draw` and
`DrawSkinned` overload keeps working and draws as static. `CharacterAvatar`, `Scene3DBinder` and `SkinnedLimb` key
themselves. The tile-world seam carries descriptors too: `ITileWorldScene.DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw)` and
`ITileWorldScene.DrawSkinned(in SkinnedInstanceDraw, ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4>)`, forwarded by `Scene3DTileWorldScene`,
let a tile-world game key its bodies.
`Scene3D.CameraCut()` resets history on a teleport or a cut, and history also resets on a resize, a preset or mode
change, a device reset and a camera jump beyond `Post.Temporal.CutDistanceMetres` or `CutAngleDegrees`.
`Scene3D.DebugView` shows `MotionVectors` under any mode and `History`, `Disocclusion` and `Reactive` under temporal
anti-aliasing. `Scene3D.LastTemporalDiagnostics` reports the frame, the jitter, key use and collisions, history
validity and the last reset reason, the internal and display sizes and the preset, and
`Scene3D.RequestTemporalCounts()` samples disoccluded, reactive and clipped pixel counts on request.

With temporal anti-aliasing off nothing of it is created and every frame renders byte-identically to <PREVIOUS> on
Metal, Direct3D 11 and Vulkan.
```

## Group I: Grimhollow adopts temporal anti-aliasing

### Contract amendment (group C, engine): the tile-world scene seam carries the rigid descriptor

Grimhollow never calls `Scene3D.Draw` for a moving body. Every body part goes through the engine seam
`KhaozEngine.TileWorld.ITileWorldScene`: `HumanoidBody.Queue` (`Grimhollow.Core/Client/HumanoidBody.cs:257-266`),
`QuadrupedBody.Queue` (`Grimhollow.Core/Client/QuadrupedBody.cs:505-514`) and `RigidMonsterBody.Draw`
(`Grimhollow.Core/Client/RigidMonsterBody.cs:54-63`) call `DrawMesh` and `DrawMeshDissolved`
(`KhaozEngine.TileWorld.Render3D/ITileWorldScene.cs:55,66`), and `Scene3DTileWorldScene` forwards them to the
plain `Scene3D.Draw` overloads (`ITileWorldScene.cs:219,225-226`). The seam has no member that carries a
`MotionKey`, and the game's headless doubles (`Grimhollow.Tests/World/FakeTileWorldScene.cs`,
`Grimhollow.Tests/Client/HumanoidBodyDissolveTests.cs:63-81`) record the seam, not the scene. Round 3 cannot key a
single body without the seam member, and a game-side downcast to `Scene3DTileWorldScene.Scene` would blind every
headless test and breaks the engine-first boundary in `AGENTS.md`.

Group C adds, in Task C9:

```csharp
// KhaozEngine.TileWorld.Render3D/ITileWorldScene.cs, interface ITileWorldScene
/// <summary>Queues one rigid mesh from a full descriptor, motion key included. Defaults to the plain and
/// dissolved members, which drop the key and every knob they cannot express, so an implementation written
/// before descriptors keeps compiling and keeps drawing. A shadow-only descriptor draws nothing.</summary>
void DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw draw)
{
    if (draw.ShadowOnly) return;
    if (draw.Dissolve > 0f)
        DrawMeshDissolved(draw.Mesh, draw.World, draw.Dissolve, draw.DissolveEdgeWidth, draw.DissolveEdgeColor);
    else DrawMesh(draw.Mesh, draw.World);
}

/// <summary>Queues one skinned mesh from a full descriptor. Defaults to the tinted and dissolved skinned
/// members.</summary>
void DrawSkinned(in SkinnedInstanceDraw draw, ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> boneMatrices)
{
    if (draw.Dissolve > 0f)
        DrawSkinnedDissolved(draw.Mesh, boneMatrices, draw.Model, draw.Tint, draw.Dissolve,
            draw.DissolveEdgeWidth, draw.DissolveEdgeColor);
    else DrawSkinned(draw.Mesh, boneMatrices, draw.Model, draw.Tint);
}

// Scene3DTileWorldScene
/// <inheritdoc />
public void DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw draw) => _scene.Draw(in draw);

/// <inheritdoc />
public void DrawSkinned(in SkinnedInstanceDraw draw, ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> boneMatrices) =>
    _scene.DrawSkinned(in draw, boneMatrices);
```

The rigid member is required by round 3. The skinned member is not consumed by round 3 but keeps the seam
symmetric for the rigged player (Grimhollow #64, worktree `feature/rigged-player-asset`). Group C's test proves the
default body reaches the plain members and that `Scene3DTileWorldScene.DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw)` reaches
`Scene3D.Draw(in RigidInstanceDraw)` with the key intact (`QueuedInstancesForTests` holds one instance whose
`Motion` is the key after one keyed draw). The engine CHANGELOG entry names both members. Task I1's
`TemporalSeamTests` finds both by reflection, so it fails the Grimhollow test run, not the build, if either the member
or the `Scene3DTileWorldScene` override is missing from the release. If the
release ships without them, group I stops at I1 and asks the owner, per the engine-first rule.

### Spec amendment (resolve spec, round 3 item 1): carcasses are keyed

Round 3 item 1 calls carcasses static. They are not while they fall: `HollowmereSession.AdvanceCarcasses`
(`Grimhollow.Core/Client/HollowmereSession.Carcasses.cs:93-137`) advances a collapse from the dead cow's last gait to
`CarcassPresentation.RestingPose` over `CarcassPresentation.CollapseSeconds = 0.9f`
(`Grimhollow.Core/Client/CarcassPresentation.cs:13`), and the thickness scale shrinks with it. Round 3 keys a carcass
from its own net id for its whole life. After the collapse the key reports zero object motion, which is what an
unkeyed draw reports, so keying it costs nothing. The resolve spec's Plan amendments already record it (item 11).

### Preamble

Group I runs in Grimhollow on the released engine. It pins the release (the engine version group H's Task H5 chooses
at release time by the ride rule, written `20.6.0` below because engine `main` stages an untagged `20.6.0`, the journal
reset, at planning time, and every command reads it from `V`), keys
every moving body part with `MotionKey.Combine(MotionKey.From(netId), part)` through the amended seam, cuts the
temporal history on a teleport and
the F8 camera flip, adds `TAA` to `Anti-aliasing` and a `Render quality` row that is dimmed and inert
unless `TAA` is chosen, extends the throwaway shimmer probe with a moving-camera mode, measures `FXAA`, `MSAA 4x` and
`TAA` at each preset on the town, forest and meadow paths, sets the default by the spec's rule, and records it in
the ledger, the development guide and the staged player changelog. The owner's windowed playtest confirms the
default. The agent never launches the client and ends I11 with a copy-ready command. Risks, in order: the seam
amendment has to be in the release or nothing can be keyed. `TAA` sizes its internal target from the window
(`RenderScale.Temporal`), while `FXAA` and `MSAA 4x` keep the fixed 1600x900 target, so on the owner's
3456x2234 display even `Performance` (1728x1117) shades more pixels than today and the "beats MSAA 4x frame time"
line may fail there even where it passes at 2560x1440. `Ultra Performance`, the engine's fifth preset
(`TemporalUpscale.UltraPerformance`, a third per axis, 72 jitter phases), renders 1152x745 there, fewer pixels than
1600x900, so the row offers it and the probe measures it. The raw flip metric counts content sliding past a pixel
under a moving camera, so the default rule reads a camera-compensated version of the same metric, proven equal to
the raw one on a still camera. The owner's settings file already stores `MSAA 4x` explicitly, so a default change
reaches only new files, and the handoff tells the owner to pick `TAA` by hand. Two files sit near the 800-line

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Tests/World/TemporalSeamTests.cs
using System.Reflection;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld;

namespace Grimhollow.Tests.World;

/// <summary>The engine surface the temporal adoption stands on. Every Grimhollow body draws through the tile-world
/// scene seam rather than through <see cref="Scene3D"/>, so the seam has to carry the rigid descriptor, and the
/// shipped seam has to hand it to the scene rather than fall back to the keyless default body.</summary>
public sealed class TemporalSeamTests
{
    static readonly Type[] RigidDescriptor = [typeof(RigidInstanceDraw).MakeByRefType()];

    [Fact]
    public void TheTileWorldSeamCarriesTheRigidDescriptor() =>
        Assert.NotNull(typeof(ITileWorldScene).GetMethod(nameof(ITileWorldScene.DrawMesh), RigidDescriptor));

    [Fact]
    public void TheShippedSeamForwardsTheDescriptorItself()
    {
        MethodInfo? own = typeof(Scene3DTileWorldScene).GetMethod(nameof(ITileWorldScene.DrawMesh),
            BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly, RigidDescriptor);

        Assert.NotNull(own);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void TheEngineOffersTemporalAntiAliasingAndFivePresets()
    {
        Assert.Equal(AntiAliasingMode.Temporal, AntiAliasing.Temporal.Mode);
        Assert.Equal(
            [TemporalUpscale.Native, TemporalUpscale.Quality, TemporalUpscale.Balanced, TemporalUpscale.Performance,
                TemporalUpscale.UltraPerformance],
            Enum.GetValues<TemporalUpscale>());
    }

    [Fact]
    public void AMotionKeyCombinesStablyAndNoneStaysNone()
    {
        MotionKey body = MotionKey.From(42UL);

        Assert.NotEqual(MotionKey.Combine(body, 3u), MotionKey.Combine(body, 4u));
        Assert.True(MotionKey.Combine(MotionKey.None, 3u).IsNone);
        Assert.True(MotionKey.From(0UL).IsNone);
    }
}
```

```markdown
### `20.6.0` (temporal anti-aliasing, upscaling and motion keys)

Swept released `20.6.0` after `20.5.1`, for [KhaozEngine #1149](https://github.com/APKiwiOrg/KhaozEngine/issues/1149),
the journal reset it carries ([KhaozEngine #1150](https://github.com/APKiwiOrg/KhaozEngine/issues/1150)) included. The pin, `ke-tileedit`, `ke-sfxbake` and all 196 vendored package
files move together. Every vendored `20.6.0`
nupkg that carries code names tag commit `1a2b3c4d` in its repository metadata. The Release solution builds with zero
warnings on this pin. With `FXAA` or `MSAA 4x` selected the engine creates no temporal target, pipeline or buffer
and the jitter is zero, so the bump alone changes no frame. The 30 avatar goldens pass unchanged on native Metal.

- **Frame view and sub-pixel jitter: TRANSITIVE through `Scene3D`.** Every draw rasterises through the frame's view
  snapshot. Culling, shadow fitting, picking and `WorldToScreen` read the unjittered view, so clicks, plates and
  hitsplats do not move under TAA.
- **`Scene3D.CameraCut`: ADOPTING.** A teleport and the F8 camera flip cut the history.
- **Automatic cuts, `Post.Temporal.CutDistanceMetres` and `CutAngleDegrees`: TRANSITIVE at the engine defaults,
  16 m and 60 degrees.** The orbit camera never moves that far in one frame except on a teleport, which cuts anyway.
- **`MotionKey`, `RigidInstanceDraw` and `Scene3D.Draw(in RigidInstanceDraw)`: ADOPTING through the tile-world seam.**
- **`ITileWorldScene.DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw)` and its `Scene3DTileWorldScene` forwarder: ADOPTING.** Every
  body draws through the seam. `TemporalSeamTests` fails the test run if either is missing. The default body still
  reaches the plain members, which `HumanoidBodyDissolveTests.SceneWithoutADissolveOverrideGetsTheDefaultSolidDrawFallback`
  pins.
- **`SkinnedInstanceDraw`, `Scene3D.DrawSkinned(in SkinnedInstanceDraw, ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4>)` and the seam's skinned descriptor:
  NOT APPLICABLE until the rigged player ([#64](https://github.com/APKiwiOrg/Grimhollow/issues/64)).** No client code
  draws a skinned mesh.
- **`CharacterAvatar` and `Scene3DBinder` keying themselves: NOT APPLICABLE.** Grimhollow uses neither (grep 0).
- **Per-path motion vectors, foliage wind at the previous frame's time included: TRANSITIVE through
  `TileWorldView`.** The short cover and the ten animated grass props report their own sway under TAA with no game
  code.
- **`TemporalHistory` resets on a size, render scale, anti-aliasing or device change: TRANSITIVE.**
- **`Scene3D.DebugView` and `SceneDebugView`: AVAILABLE.** No Grimhollow toggle sets it. It is the quickest way to
  see a body that forgot its key.
- **`Scene3D.LastTemporalDiagnostics`: AVAILABLE.** The shimmer probe prints it. The F1 overlay does not.
- **`AntiAliasing.Temporal` and `AntiAliasingMode.Temporal`: ADOPTING as `TAA`.**
- **`RenderScale.Temporal`: TRANSITIVE under `TAA`.** TAA sizes its internal target from the window times the render
  quality instead of the fixed 1600x900 target `FXAA` and `MSAA 4x` keep.
- **`TemporalUpscale` and `Post.Temporal.Upscale`: ADOPTING as `Render quality`.**
- **`TemporalUpscale.UltraPerformance`: ADOPTING as `Ultra Performance`.** A third of the window per axis, the one
  preset that shades fewer pixels than 1600x900 on the owner's 3456x2234 display.
- **`Post.Temporal.UpscaleRatio`: AVAILABLE.** Settings offers the five presets only.
- **`Post.Temporal.Sharpness`: TRANSITIVE at the engine default, 0.25.**
- **`Post.Temporal.MipBiasOffset`: TRANSITIVE at the engine default, -0.5.**
- **Reactive estimate for transparent content: TRANSITIVE.** The level-up sparks and the river take a lower history
  weight under TAA.
- **Distortion after the resolve: NOT APPLICABLE.** Grimhollow draws no distortion (grep 0).
- **The screen-fixed starfield taking zero motion: NOT APPLICABLE.** The viewer turns the starfield off and draws the
  sky (`HollowmereViewer`), which keeps the rotation reprojection, so its sun holds its place in the world as the
  camera turns.
- **The edge outline running ahead of the resolve: NOT APPLICABLE.** `Post.Outline` is off in Grimhollow.
- **MSAA refused while temporal is active: NOT APPLICABLE.** The game's choices are exclusive.
```

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Tests/World/FakeTileWorldSceneMotionTests.cs
using System.Numerics;
using KhaozEngine.Primitives;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld;

namespace Grimhollow.Tests.World;

/// <summary>The recording scene keeps the motion key the seam's descriptor member hands it and records the plain
/// members as unkeyed, so a body test can tell a keyed part from a static one.</summary>
public sealed class FakeTileWorldSceneMotionTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void ADescriptorDrawKeepsItsKeyAndFillsTheListsThePlainMembersFill()
    {
        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();
        ITileWorldScene seam = scene;
        var handle = new MeshHandle(7);
        Matrix4x4 world = Matrix4x4.CreateTranslation(1f, 2f, 3f);
        MotionKey key = MotionKey.Combine(MotionKey.From(42UL), 3u);

        seam.DrawMesh(new RigidInstanceDraw(handle, world) { Motion = key });
        seam.DrawMesh(new RigidInstanceDraw(handle, world)
        {
            Dissolve = .5f,
            DissolveEdgeWidth = 0f,
            DissolveEdgeColor = Color.Transparent,
            Motion = key,
        });

        Assert.Equal([world, world], scene.Drawn);
        Assert.Equal(.5f, Assert.Single(scene.Dissolved).Dissolve);
        Assert.Equal([key, key], scene.Motions.Select(draw => draw.Motion));
        Assert.Equal([handle, handle], scene.Motions.Select(draw => draw.Handle));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void ThePlainMembersRecordNoKeyAndAFrameClearForgetsThem()
    {
        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();

        scene.DrawMesh(new MeshHandle(1), Matrix4x4.Identity);
        scene.DrawMeshDissolved(new MeshHandle(2), Matrix4x4.Identity, .25f, 0f, Color.Transparent);

        Assert.Equal(2, scene.Motions.Count);
        Assert.All(scene.Motions, draw => Assert.True(draw.Motion.IsNone));

        scene.ClearFrame();
        Assert.Empty(scene.Motions);
    }
}
```

```csharp
    /// <summary>Every rigid draw since the last <see cref="ClearFrame"/>, in submission order, with the motion key it
```

```csharp
    /// <summary>Records one ground-mesh draw at its world transform, unkeyed.</summary>
    public void DrawMesh(MeshHandle handle, Matrix4x4 world)
    {
        Drawn.Add(world);
        Motions.Add((handle, world, MotionKey.None));
    }

    /// <summary>Records one dissolved mesh draw, unkeyed, and includes it in the complete draw list.</summary>
    public void DrawMeshDissolved(MeshHandle handle, Matrix4x4 world, float dissolve, float edgeWidth,
        Color edgeColor)
    {
        Drawn.Add(world);
        Dissolved.Add((handle, world, dissolve, edgeWidth, edgeColor));
        Motions.Add((handle, world, MotionKey.None));
    }

    /// <summary>Records one descriptor draw into the lists the plain members fill, a dissolve above zero counting
    /// as a dissolved draw, and keeps the motion key it carried.</summary>
    public void DrawMesh(in RigidInstanceDraw draw)
    {
        Drawn.Add(draw.World);
        if (draw.Dissolve > 0f)
            Dissolved.Add((draw.Mesh, draw.World, draw.Dissolve, draw.DissolveEdgeWidth, draw.DissolveEdgeColor));
        Motions.Add((draw.Mesh, draw.World, draw.Motion));
    }
```

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Tests/Client/BodyMotionKeyTests.cs
using System.Numerics;
using Grimhollow.Core.Client;
using Grimhollow.Shared;
using Grimhollow.Tests.Content;
using Grimhollow.Tests.World;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld.Netcode;

namespace Grimhollow.Tests.Client;

/// <summary>Every moving body part draws under a motion key that is its own and the same on every frame, so the
/// engine can find where that part was last frame. A key comes from the body's net id and the part's place in the
/// body, never from draw order, so two bodies sharing one mesh set never share a key.</summary>
public partial class BodyMotionKeyTests
{
    static GltfMeshResolver Resolver() =>
        new(HollowmereWorldPaths.ModelDirectory, new GreyboxMeshResolver(1f, 3f));

    static MotionKey[] Keys(FakeTileWorldScene scene) => scene.Motions.Select(draw => draw.Motion).ToArray();

    static Matrix4x4[] Worlds(FakeTileWorldScene scene) => scene.Motions.Select(draw => draw.World).ToArray();

    [Fact]
    public void EveryAvatarPartAndHeldPieceKeepsItsOwnKeyFromOneFrameToTheNext()
    {
        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();
        GltfMeshResolver meshes = Resolver();
        using var avatar = new AvatarMesh(scene, meshes);
        using var held = new HeldItemMeshes(scene, meshes, TestContentReads.Content);
        HeldPiece sword = held.ForMeshRef(HeldItemMeshes.SwordMeshRef);
        HeldPiece shield = held.ForMeshRef(HeldItemMeshes.ShieldMeshRef);
        MotionKey body = BodyMotion.ForBody(42);

        scene.ClearFrame();
        avatar.Draw(new TilePose(new Vector3(30f, 3f, -44f), 0f), WalkPose.Rest, sword, shield, default, 1f, body);
        MotionKey[] first = Keys(scene);
        Matrix4x4[] before = Worlds(scene);
        scene.ClearFrame();
        avatar.Draw(new TilePose(new Vector3(30.4f, 3f, -44f), .3f), new WalkPose(.4f, -.4f, -.3f, .3f), sword,
            shield, default, 1f, body);

        Assert.Equal(avatar.PartCount + sword.Parts!.Count + shield.Parts!.Count, first.Length);
        Assert.Equal(first, Keys(scene));
        Assert.Equal(first.Length, first.Distinct().Count());
        Assert.DoesNotContain(MotionKey.None, first);
        Assert.NotEqual(before, Worlds(scene));
    }

    public void TwoBodiesDrawnThroughTheSameMeshesNeverShareAKey()
    {
        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();
        using var avatar = new AvatarMesh(scene, Resolver());
        var pose = new TilePose(new Vector3(30f, 3f, -44f), 0f);

        scene.ClearFrame();
        avatar.Draw(pose, WalkPose.Rest, default, default, default, 1f, BodyMotion.ForBody(7));
        avatar.Draw(pose, WalkPose.Rest, default, default, default, 1f, BodyMotion.ForBody(8));
        MotionKey[] keys = Keys(scene);

        Assert.Equal(2 * avatar.PartCount, keys.Length);
        Assert.Equal(keys.Length, keys.Distinct().Count());
    }
```

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Core/Client/BodyMotion.cs
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Numerics;
using KhaozEngine.Primitives;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld;

namespace Grimhollow.Core.Client;

/// <summary>The motion keys a moving body draws under, and the one queue every rigid body part goes through.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// A body's key comes from its replicated net id. The server hands those out from one counter that starts at 1 and
/// never reuses an id, so the key holds for as long as the body is in view and no two bodies share one. Each piece
/// takes <c>Combine(body, slot)</c> and each mesh part inside it <c>Combine(piece, part)</c>, so bodies drawn
/// through one shared mesh set (every player shares one <see cref="AvatarMesh"/>) still key every part apart. A
/// draw handed <see cref="MotionKey.None"/> stays unkeyed all the way down, which is what the art captures and the
/// tests that do not care pass.
/// </remarks>
internal static class BodyMotion
{
    /// <summary>The weapon hand's held piece, the slot after a humanoid's ten composed pieces.</summary>
    internal const int RightHandSlot = HumanoidBody.PieceCount;

    /// <summary>The off hand's held piece.</summary>
    internal const int LeftHandSlot = RightHandSlot + 1;

    /// <summary>The piece worn around the right wrist.</summary>
    internal const int RightWristSlot = LeftHandSlot + 1;

    /// <summary>The key for one replicated body. Net ids start at 1, so anything else names no body and stays
    /// unkeyed.</summary>
    /// <param name="netId">The body's net id, local or remote, or a carcass's own id.</param>
    internal static MotionKey ForBody(long netId) => netId > 0 ? MotionKey.From((ulong)netId) : MotionKey.None;

    /// <summary>The key for one piece of a body. A body with no key gives pieces with no key.</summary>
    /// <param name="body">The body's key.</param>
    /// <param name="slot">The piece's index in its body, or one of the held slots.</param>
    internal static MotionKey ForPiece(MotionKey body, int slot) => MotionKey.Combine(body, (uint)slot);

    /// <summary>Queues one piece's mesh parts at one transform, each under its own key. A dissolve of zero is the
    /// solid draw and anything else folds its discard into the shared model fragment, the same two draws the seam's
    /// plain members make. The key rides beside them and changes the motion target and nothing else.</summary>
    /// <param name="scene">The scene seam.</param>
    /// <param name="parts">The piece's uploaded parts.</param>
    /// <param name="world">The piece's transform this frame.</param>
    /// <param name="dissolve">The dissolve threshold, 0 for solid.</param>
    /// <param name="piece">The piece's key, from <see cref="ForPiece"/>.</param>
    internal static void Queue(ITileWorldScene scene, IReadOnlyList<MeshHandle> parts, in Matrix4x4 world,
        float dissolve, MotionKey piece)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < parts.Count; i++)
        {
            MotionKey motion = MotionKey.Combine(piece, (uint)i);
            RigidInstanceDraw draw = dissolve > 0f
                ? new RigidInstanceDraw(parts[i], world)
                {
                    Dissolve = dissolve,
                    DissolveEdgeWidth = 0f,
                    DissolveEdgeColor = Color.Transparent,
                    Motion = motion,
                }
                : new RigidInstanceDraw(parts[i], world) { Motion = motion };
            scene.DrawMesh(in draw);
        }
    }
}
```

In `Grimhollow.Core/Client/HumanoidBody.cs`, replace lines 216-245 (the wrist overload of `Draw`) with:

```csharp
    /// <summary>Queues the body, its held pieces and a wrap on the right forearm, every part under its own key.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="pose">Where and which way to draw, already centred on its tile by the presenter.</param>
    /// <param name="walk">This frame's limb angles.</param>
    /// <param name="rightHand">The weapon hand's piece. Default for an empty hand.</param>
    /// <param name="leftHand">The off hand's piece. Default for an empty hand.</param>
    /// <param name="rightWrist">A piece wrapped around the right wrist. Default for none.</param>
    /// <param name="visibility">How visible the body is, 0 through 1, as for the overload above.</param>
    /// <param name="motion">The body's key, from <see cref="BodyMotion.ForBody"/>. Every piece and held piece draws
    /// under a key derived from it. Default draws the body unkeyed.</param>
    public void Draw(in TilePose pose, in WalkPose walk, in HeldPiece rightHand, in HeldPiece leftHand,
        in HeldPiece rightWrist, float visibility, MotionKey motion = default)
    {
        if (_disposed || PartCount == 0) return;
        float dissolve = DissolveFor(visibility);
        // A fully dissolved body is every piece the fragment shader discards whole, so it costs a composition
        // and a draw apiece to put nothing on the screen. Unreachable from this game's own draw, which skips a
        // body at a weight of zero before it gets here, but this is public API and the caller's zero is the
        // caller's business.
        if (dissolve >= 1f) return;
        Span<Matrix4x4> at = stackalloc Matrix4x4[PieceCount];
        Compose(Rig, pose, walk, at);
        for (int piece = 0; piece < _pieces.Length; piece++)
            BodyMotion.Queue(_scene, _pieces[piece], at[piece], dissolve, BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, piece));
        // Each held piece rides the FOREARM's transform, not the body's and not the upper arm's, so it swings
        // with the fist that holds it through the elbow as well as the shoulder.
        // EACH HAND TAKES ITS OWN, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT AXES. The weapon hand TIPS its piece about the
        // hand's own x, which is what points a blade's head. The off hand TURNS its piece about the BODY's
        // vertical through the fist, which is what swings a shield's face off the body's side and round to
        // face whatever the body faces (AvatarSockets.OffTurn). Both are identity at zero, so a body with
        // neither draws exactly as it always did.
        DrawHeld(rightHand, at[ForearmRight], walk.RightWrist, 0f, dissolve,
            BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, BodyMotion.RightHandSlot));
        DrawHeld(leftHand, at[ForearmLeft], 0f, walk.LeftWrist, dissolve,
            BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, BodyMotion.LeftHandSlot));
        if (!rightWrist.IsEmpty)
        {
            Matrix4x4 wrist = rightWrist.Local
                * Matrix4x4.CreateTranslation(Rig.HandFromElbow) * at[ForearmRight];
            BodyMotion.Queue(_scene, rightWrist.Parts!, wrist, dissolve,
                BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, BodyMotion.RightWristSlot));
        }
    }
```

```csharp
    /// <summary>Queues the whole body for this frame with a fighting stroke laid over its gait.</summary>
    /// <param name="pose">Where and which way to draw, already centred on its footprint by the presenter.</param>
    /// <param name="walk">This frame's biped-shaped pose, for the lean and the breath.</param>
    /// <param name="gait">This frame's cycle, from <see cref="WalkCycle.Sample"/>.</param>
    /// <param name="strike">Where the body is in its headbutt and how much of it is drawn, from
    /// <c>HollowmereSession.StrikeOf</c>. <see cref="QuadrupedStrike.None"/> is the plain draw.</param>
    /// <param name="visibility">How visible the body is, 0 through 1. See <see cref="HumanoidBody.Draw"/>.</param>
    /// <param name="motion">The body's key, from <see cref="BodyMotion.ForBody"/>. Default draws unkeyed.</param>
    public void Draw(in TilePose pose, in WalkPose walk, in GaitSample gait, in QuadrupedStrike strike,
        float visibility = 1f, MotionKey motion = default)
    {
        if (_disposed || PartCount == 0) return;
        float dissolve = HumanoidBody.DissolveFor(visibility);
        if (dissolve >= 1f) return;
        Span<Matrix4x4> at = stackalloc Matrix4x4[PieceCount];
        Compose(Rig, pose, walk, PoseFor(Rig, gait, strike), at);
        for (int piece = 0; piece < _pieces.Length; piece++)
            BodyMotion.Queue(_scene, _pieces[piece], at[piece], dissolve, BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, piece));
    }

    /// <summary>Queues the full-size body through the engine quadruped collapse composition, under the carcass's
    /// own motion key. The collapse moves the pieces for <see cref="CarcassPresentation.CollapseSeconds"/>.</summary>
    public void DrawCarcass(in TilePose pose, in EngineQuadrupedPose carcass, float thicknessScale,
        float collapseProgress, float visibility = 1f, MotionKey motion = default)
    {
        if (_disposed || PartCount == 0) return;
        float dissolve = HumanoidBody.DissolveFor(visibility);
        if (dissolve >= 1f) return;
        Span<Matrix4x4> at = stackalloc Matrix4x4[CarcassPieceCount];
        ComposeCarcass(pose, carcass, thicknessScale, collapseProgress, at);
        for (int piece = 0; piece < CarcassPieceCount; piece++)
            BodyMotion.Queue(_scene, CarcassParts(piece), at[piece], dissolve, BodyMotion.ForPiece(motion, piece));
    }
```

```csharp
    public void Draw(in TilePose pose, in WalkPose walk, in GaitSample gait, in QuadrupedStrike strike,
```

```csharp
    /// <summary>Frames the harness until <paramref name="done"/> holds, at most 240 frames, then asserts it.</summary>
    public static void WaitUntil(this LoopbackHarness harness, Func<bool> done)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < 240 && !done(); i++) harness.Frames(1);
        Assert.True(done());
    }

    /// <summary>Spawns a cow on <paramref name="tile"/> and waits until the session knows its kind and pose.</summary>
    /// <returns>The cow's net id.</returns>
    public static long SpawnCow(this LoopbackHarness harness, TileCoord tile)
    {

            new TileActorSpawn(20, GrimhollowProtocol.AttackTicks, TileDirection.S));
        Assert.True(GrimhollowActorComponents.TryWrite(harness.Server, cow,
            new MonsterKind { Kind = MonsterKindId.Cow }));
        harness.WaitUntil(() => harness.Session.MonsterKindOf(cow) == MonsterKindId.Cow
            && harness.Session.Client.TryGetRemotePose(cow, out _));
        return cow;

            DeathUtcTicks = now.Ticks,
            PublicUtcTicks = now.AddSeconds(60).Ticks,
            ExpiresUtcTicks = now.AddSeconds(180).Ticks,
        }));
        harness.WaitUntil(() => harness.Session.CarcassCount == before + 1);
        return carcass;
    }
}
```

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Tests/Client/BodyMotionSessionTests.cs
using System.Numerics;
using Grimhollow.Core.Client;
using Grimhollow.Core.World;
using Grimhollow.Server;
using Grimhollow.Shared;
using Grimhollow.Shared.Combat;
using Grimhollow.Shared.Items;
using Grimhollow.Shared.Presentation;
using Grimhollow.Tests.Content;
using Grimhollow.Tests.World;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld;
using KhaozEngine.TileWorld.Netcode;
using EngineQuadrupedPose = KhaozEngine.SegmentRig.QuadrupedPose;

namespace Grimhollow.Tests.Client;

/// <summary>The session's draw pass keys the local player, a monster and a carcass from their own net ids, the same
/// keys every frame, and the static world and the drops on it draw unkeyed.</summary>
public class BodyMotionSessionTests
{
    static GltfMeshResolver Resolver() =>
        new(HollowmereWorldPaths.ModelDirectory, new GreyboxMeshResolver(1f, 3f));

    static List<MotionKey> KeysOf(FakeTileWorldScene scene, Action draw)
    {
        scene.ClearFrame();
        draw();
        return scene.Motions.Select(entry => entry.Motion).ToList();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void TheSessionKeysEachBodyAndCarcassByItsOwnNetId()
    {
        TileCoord cowTile = new(24, 24, 0);
        using var harness = new LoopbackHarness(new TileCoord(20, 20, 0));
        harness.Frames(24);
        long cow = harness.SpawnCow(cowTile);

        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();
        GltfMeshResolver meshes = Resolver();
        using var avatar = new AvatarMesh(scene, meshes);
        using var monsters = new MonsterMeshes(scene, meshes);
        monsters.RegisterBounds(harness.Session);
        MonsterMesh cowBody = Assert.IsType<MonsterMesh>(monsters.For(MonsterKindId.Cow));
        var anywhere = new TilePose(Vector3.Zero, 0f);
        long local = harness.Session.Client.LocalNetId;
        HashSet<MotionKey> localKeys = KeysOf(scene, () => avatar.Draw(anywhere, WalkPose.Rest, default, default,
            default, 1f, BodyMotion.ForBody(local))).ToHashSet();
        HashSet<MotionKey> livingKeys = KeysOf(scene, () => cowBody.Draw(anywhere, WalkPose.Rest, GaitSample.Still,
            QuadrupedStrike.None, 1f, BodyMotion.ForBody(cow))).ToHashSet();

        List<MotionKey> first = KeysOf(scene, () => harness.Session.DrawAvatars(avatar, monsters));
        harness.Frames(6);
        List<MotionKey> second = KeysOf(scene, () => harness.Session.DrawAvatars(avatar, monsters));

        Assert.DoesNotContain(MotionKey.None, first);
        Assert.Equal(first.Count, first.Distinct().Count());
        Assert.True(localKeys.IsSubsetOf(first));
        Assert.True(livingKeys.IsSubsetOf(first));
        Assert.False(localKeys.Overlaps(livingKeys));
        Assert.True(first.ToHashSet().SetEquals(second));

        long carcass = harness.SpawnCowCarcass(cowTile, cow);
        HashSet<MotionKey> carcassKeys = KeysOf(scene, () => cowBody.DrawCarcass(anywhere, EngineQuadrupedPose.Rest,
            1f, 1f, 1f, BodyMotion.ForBody(carcass))).ToHashSet();

        List<MotionKey> dead = KeysOf(scene, () => harness.Session.DrawAvatars(avatar, monsters));

        Assert.True(carcassKeys.IsSubsetOf(dead));
        Assert.False(livingKeys.Overlaps(dead));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void DropsAndTheAuthoredWorldDrawUnkeyed()
    {
        var scene = new FakeTileWorldScene();
        using var drops = new GroundItemMeshes(scene, Resolver(), TestContentReads.Content);
        var document = new TileWorldDocument();
        var ground = new TileDocumentGroundHeight(document);

        scene.ClearFrame();
        drops.Draw(ground, document.TileSize,
            [(11L, new TileGroundItem { ItemId = ItemId.Logs, Count = 1, X = 4, Z = 4, Plane = 0 })], plane: 0);

        Assert.NotEmpty(scene.Motions);
        Assert.All(scene.Motions, draw => Assert.True(draw.Motion.IsNone));

        using var world = new HollowmereWorld(KitMeshes.Content("worlds", "hollowmere"), scene);
        world.Prime(new TileCoord(95, 73, 0));
        scene.ClearFrame();
        world.Draw(new Vector3(95f, 0f, -73f));

        Assert.NotEmpty(scene.Motions);
        Assert.All(scene.Motions, draw => Assert.True(draw.Motion.IsNone));
    }
}
```

```csharp
    [InlineData(GrimhollowRenderQuality.Performance, GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced)]
    [InlineData(GrimhollowRenderQuality.UltraPerformance, GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality)]
    public void RenderQualityGoesToDiskAndComesBackOnTheNextLoad(
        GrimhollowRenderQuality choice, GrimhollowRenderQuality previous)
    {
        using PersistenceQueue queue = new();
        using (GrimhollowSettingsStore store = new(Storage(queue)))
        {
            store.RenderQuality = previous;
            store.RenderQuality = choice;
            queue.Flush();
        }

        using GrimhollowSettingsStore reopened = new(Storage(queue));

        Assert.Equal(choice, reopened.RenderQuality);
        Assert.Equal(choice, reopened.Settings.RenderQuality);
    }

        Assert.Equal(GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.DefaultRenderQuality, store.Settings.RenderQuality);

        store.RenderQuality = GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.DefaultRenderQuality;
```

```csharp
/// <summary>The 3D scene anti-aliasing choices offered by the game. Mapped to the engine's selection in
/// <see cref="GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings"/> and nowhere else. Persisted by number, so a new choice is appended.
/// </summary>
public enum GrimhollowAntiAliasing
{
    /// <summary>The FXAA post pass alone, the lighter option. Distant grass stops swaying sooner under it,
    /// because FXAA alone steadies less of the far shimmer.</summary>
    Fxaa,

    /// <summary>Four-sample MSAA with FXAA after the resolve, for steadier distant grass and fine edges at a
    /// small cost to frame rate.</summary>
    Msaa4,

    /// <summary>Temporal anti-aliasing with upscaling at the player's <see cref="GrimhollowRenderQuality"/>. It holds
    /// thin distant detail such as grass steady while the camera moves.</summary>
    Taa,
}

/// <summary>How far below the window TAA renders before it rebuilds the full image. Mapped to the engine's preset in
/// <see cref="GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings"/> and nowhere else, and read only while TAA is selected.</summary>
public enum GrimhollowRenderQuality
{
    /// <summary>The window's own size.</summary>
    Native,

    /// <summary>Two thirds of the window on each axis.</summary>
    Quality,

    /// <summary>About 59 percent of the window on each axis.</summary>
    Balanced,

    /// <summary>Half the window on each axis.</summary>
    Performance,

    /// <summary>A third of the window on each axis, for very dense displays: at 3456x2234 it renders fewer pixels
    /// than the fixed 1600x900 target FXAA and MSAA 4x use.</summary>
    UltraPerformance,
}
```

```csharp
using System;
using KhaozEngine.Render3D;

namespace Grimhollow.Core.Config;

/// <summary>The one home of what the player's anti-aliasing choice means: the engine's scene selection, the TAA
/// render quality that goes with it, and the grass wind fade. The viewer seeds the scene and the grass through it,
/// the settings screen's live change goes through it, and the art captures read its default so they keep matching
/// the live default look.</summary>
public static class GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings
{
    /// <summary>The choice a new or older settings file takes.</summary>
    public const GrimhollowAntiAliasing DefaultChoice = GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Msaa4;

    /// <summary>The render quality a new or older settings file takes. Read only while TAA is selected.</summary>
    /// <remarks>Quality renders two thirds of the window on each axis, 1707x960 at a 2560x1440 window, the lightest
    /// preset that still shades at least as many pixels as the fixed 1600x900 target FXAA and MSAA 4x render at. The
    /// moving-camera probe sets the shipped value.</remarks>
    public const GrimhollowRenderQuality DefaultRenderQuality = GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality;

    /// <summary>The engine selection for <see cref="DefaultChoice"/>.</summary>
    public static AntiAliasing Default => EngineValue(DefaultChoice);

    /// <summary>The engine selection one of the game's choices names.</summary>
    /// <param name="choice">The player's choice. Unknown values take the FXAA path, which every device runs.
    /// The settings store normalizes them to <see cref="DefaultChoice"/> before they get here.</param>
    /// <remarks>MSAA is clamped to the device by the engine when it builds its targets, so a device without
    /// four samples degrades rather than failing.</remarks>
    public static AntiAliasing EngineValue(GrimhollowAntiAliasing choice) => choice switch
    {
        GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Msaa4 => AntiAliasing.Msaa(4, postFxaa: true),
        GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa => AntiAliasing.Temporal,
        _ => AntiAliasing.Fxaa,
    };

    /// <summary>The engine preset one of the game's render qualities names.</summary>
    /// <param name="quality">The player's render quality. Unknown values take <see cref="DefaultRenderQuality"/>'s
    /// preset, matching what the settings store normalizes them to.</param>
    public static TemporalUpscale EngineUpscale(GrimhollowRenderQuality quality) => quality switch
    {
        GrimhollowRenderQuality.Native => TemporalUpscale.Native,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality => TemporalUpscale.Quality,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced => TemporalUpscale.Balanced,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality.Performance => TemporalUpscale.Performance,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality.UltraPerformance => TemporalUpscale.UltraPerformance,
        _ => EngineUpscale(DefaultRenderQuality),
    };

    /// <summary>The blade height in internal pixels under which grass stops swaying, for one of the game's
    /// choices. Written into the ground cover options, which the authored animated grass props share.</summary>
    /// <param name="choice">The player's choice. Unknown values take the FXAA fade, matching
    /// <see cref="EngineValue"/>.</param>
    /// <remarks>MSAA 4x already steadies distant blades, so 3 keeps over half the sway around the player. FXAA
    /// alone leaves more far flicker, and 6 cut 98.8 to 100% of it in the still-camera shimmer probe. TAA starts on
    /// MSAA 4x's 3 until the moving-camera probe measures its own.</remarks>
    public static float WindFadeBladePixels(GrimhollowAntiAliasing choice) => choice switch
    {
        GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Msaa4 => 3f,
        GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa => 3f,
        _ => 6f,
    };

    /// <summary>Writes a choice and a render quality into a scene's settings. The engine rebuilds its targets when
    /// the sample count or the temporal preset changes.</summary>
    /// <param name="post">The scene's post-process settings.</param>
    /// <param name="choice">The player's choice. Unknown values take the FXAA path.</param>
    /// <param name="quality">The player's TAA render quality.</param>
    /// <exception cref="ArgumentNullException"><paramref name="post"/> is null.</exception>
    public static void Apply(PixelPostProcessSettings post, GrimhollowAntiAliasing choice,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality quality)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(post);
        post.Quality.AntiAliasing = EngineValue(choice);
        // Written whatever the choice. The engine reads it only while TAA is selected, so a player who picks TAA
        // later gets the preset they saved.
        post.Temporal.Upscale = EngineUpscale(quality);
    }
}
```

```csharp
    /// <param name="antiAliasing">The player's saved anti-aliasing choice, for the scene and the grass wind fade.
    /// A later change in Settings arrives through <see cref="AntiAliasing"/>.</param>
    /// <param name="renderQuality">The player's saved TAA render quality, read by the scene only while TAA is
    /// selected. A later change in Settings arrives through <see cref="RenderQuality"/>.</param>
    public HollowmereViewer(Scene3D scene, string worldDirectory, float aspect,
        CameraMode bootMode = CameraMode.Player,
        GrimhollowAntiAliasing antiAliasing = GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.DefaultChoice,
        GrimhollowRenderQuality renderQuality = GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.DefaultRenderQuality)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(scene);

        // The cycle leaves background selection to its caller. Keep noon as the boot look until the first
        // authoritative world-clock state arrives.
        scene.Post.Sky.Enabled = true;
        scene.Post.Starfield = false;
        HollowmereLighting.Apply(0.5f, scene.Post);
        // The player's edge filter and TAA preset, and the grass wind fade that goes with the filter.
        GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.Apply(scene.Post, antiAliasing, renderQuality);
        _renderQuality = renderQuality;

        _world = new HollowmereWorld(worldDirectory, new Scene3DTileWorldScene(scene)) { AntiAliasing = antiAliasing };
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa`, `GrimhollowRenderQuality`, `GrimhollowSettingsStore.RenderQuality`,
  `HollowmereViewer.RenderQuality` (I7)
- Produces: `SettingsScreen(..., Action<GrimhollowAntiAliasing, GrimhollowRenderQuality>? onAntiAliasingChanged = null)`,
  `SettingsScreen.RenderQualityDropdown`, `SettingsScreen.RenderQualityLabel`, `SettingsScreen.DisabledOpacity`,
  `SettingsScreen.GraphicsRowCount == 9`, `SettingsStrings.AntiAliasingTaa`, `SettingsStrings.RenderQuality`,
  `RenderQualityNative`, `RenderQualityQuality`, `RenderQualityBalanced`, `RenderQualityPerformance`,
  `RenderQualityUltraPerformance`

Decision: the `Render quality` row is **dimmed and inert**, not hidden, while `FXAA` or `MSAA 4x` is chosen. The five
tabs share one row grid where a row index means one place on every tab (`SettingsScreen.Layout.cs:101-109`), and the
dialog height is derived from `MaxRowCount` so switching never resizes the window under the pointer
(`SettingsScreen.Layout.cs:52-55`). A row that came and went would move `Show roofs` under the pointer each time the
anti-aliasing choice changed, and the open anti-aliasing list covers the rows below it
(`SettingsScreenAntiAliasingTests.cs:73-92`), so the rows it lands on would shift between picks. A dimmed row also
tells the player TAA has a quality setting, and it keeps the saved preset for the moment TAA is chosen again. Rows go
from 8 to 9: `ContentHeight` rises by 44 to 522 and `DialogHeight` to 560 design pixels, inside the 720-high design
viewport and the 640-high resize the tests use.

```csharp
// Grimhollow.Tests/Client/SettingsScreenRenderQualityTests.cs
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Numerics;
using Grimhollow.Core.Client;
using Grimhollow.Core.Config;
using Grimhollow.Core.Localization;
using KhaozEngine.App;
using KhaozEngine.Gui;
using KhaozEngine.Primitives;

namespace Grimhollow.Tests.Client;

/// <summary>The Graphics tab's render quality row: the TAA preset, live only while TAA is the anti-aliasing choice.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>A third FILE of the same class, the <c>SettingsScreenAntiAliasingTests</c> split, on the same harness.
/// </remarks>
public partial class SettingsScreenTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void TheRenderQualityRowSitsUnderAntiAliasingAndPushesRoofsDownOneRow()
    {
        Harness harness = new();

        Rect row = SettingsScreen.RowRect(harness.Screen.DialogBounds, 7);
        Assert.Equal(row.Y, harness.Screen.RenderQualityLabel.Bounds.Y);
        Assert.Equal(row.Y, harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown.TriggerBounds.Y);
        Assert.Equal(SettingsScreen.RowRect(harness.Screen.DialogBounds, 8).Y, harness.Screen.RoofsToggle.Bounds.Y);
        Assert.Equal((int)GrimhollowAntiAliasingSettings.DefaultRenderQuality,
            harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown.SelectedValue);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void TheRenderQualitySelectorOffersNativeQualityBalancedPerformanceThenUltraPerformance()
    {
        GrimhollowLocalization.Initialize();
        IStringCatalog catalog = GrimhollowLocalization.CreateCatalog();
        Harness harness = new();

        IReadOnlyList<DropdownOption> options = harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown.Options;

        Assert.Equal([(int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.Native, (int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality,
            (int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced, (int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.Performance,
            (int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.UltraPerformance],
            options.Select(option => option.Value));
        Assert.Equal(["Native", "Quality", "Balanced", "Performance", "Ultra Performance"],
            options.Select(option => option.Content.Resolve(catalog)));
        Assert.Equal("Render quality", LocalizedText.Of(SettingsStrings.RenderQuality).Resolve(catalog));
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Fxaa)]
    [InlineData(GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Msaa4)]
    public void TheRenderQualityRowIsDimmedAndInertUnlessTaaIsChosen(GrimhollowAntiAliasing choice)
    {
        Harness harness = new(initialAntiAliasing: choice, initialRenderQuality: GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced);
        Dropdown selector = harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown;

        harness.Tap(Centre(selector.TriggerBounds));

        Assert.False(selector.IsOpen);
        Assert.Equal(SettingsScreen.DisabledOpacity, selector.Opacity);
        Assert.Equal((Vector4)GrimhollowTheme.TextDisabled, harness.Screen.RenderQualityLabel.Color);
        Assert.Equal((int)GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced, selector.SelectedValue);
        Assert.Equal(0, harness.Storage.Saves);
        Assert.Empty(harness.LiveRenderQualityRequests);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void ChoosingTaaLiftsTheRowAndLeavingTaaDimsItAgain()
    {
        Harness harness = new(initialAntiAliasing: GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Msaa4);
        Dropdown selector = harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown;

        harness.ChooseValue(harness.Screen.AntiAliasingDropdown, (int)GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa);
        Assert.Equal(1f, selector.Opacity);
        Assert.Equal(Vector4.One, harness.Screen.RenderQualityLabel.Color);
        harness.Tap(Centre(selector.TriggerBounds));
        Assert.True(selector.IsOpen);
        harness.Tap(Centre(selector.TriggerBounds));

        harness.ChooseValue(harness.Screen.AntiAliasingDropdown, (int)GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Fxaa);

        Assert.Equal(SettingsScreen.DisabledOpacity, selector.Opacity);
        Assert.False(selector.IsOpen);
    }

    [Theory]
    [InlineData(GrimhollowRenderQuality.Balanced, GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality)]
    [InlineData(GrimhollowRenderQuality.Native, GrimhollowRenderQuality.Performance)]
    public void RenderQualityChangePersistsBeforeRequestingOneLiveEngineChange(
        GrimhollowRenderQuality choice, GrimhollowRenderQuality initial)
    {
        Harness harness = new(initialAntiAliasing: GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa, initialRenderQuality: initial);

        harness.ChooseValue(harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown, (int)choice);

        Assert.Equal(choice, harness.Store.RenderQuality);
        Assert.Equal(choice, harness.ReloadSettings().RenderQuality);
        Assert.Equal(1, harness.Storage.Saves);
        Assert.Equal([GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa], harness.LiveAntiAliasingRequests);
        Assert.Equal([choice], harness.LiveRenderQualityRequests);
        Assert.Equal([choice], harness.PersistedRenderQualityAtRequest);
        Assert.Equal(0, harness.Changes);
        Assert.Equal(0, harness.DisplayChanges);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void PickingARenderQualityRowOverTheRoofsSwitchDoesNotFlipIt()
    {
        Harness harness = new(initialAntiAliasing: GrimhollowAntiAliasing.Taa,
            initialRenderQuality: GrimhollowRenderQuality.Quality);
        Dropdown selector = harness.Screen.RenderQualityDropdown;
        harness.Tap(Centre(selector.TriggerBounds));

        Rect option = selector.OptionBounds(0);
        Rect roofs = harness.Screen.RoofsToggle.Bounds;
        float left = MathF.Max(option.X, roofs.X), right = MathF.Min(option.X + option.Width, roofs.X + roofs.Width);
        float top = MathF.Max(option.Y, roofs.Y), bottom = MathF.Min(option.Y + option.Height, roofs.Y + roofs.Height);
        Assert.True(left < right && top < bottom, "The open list no longer covers the roofs switch.");
        harness.Tap(new Vector2((left + right) / 2f, (top + bottom) / 2f));

        Assert.Equal(GrimhollowRenderQuality.Native, harness.Store.RenderQuality);
        Assert.True(harness.Store.ShowRoofs);
        Assert.True(harness.Screen.RoofsToggle.IsOn);
    }
}
```

```csharp
    // changed. A dimmed row also shows the player what TAA adds, and it keeps the saved preset for the moment TAA
    // is chosen again.
    void RefreshRenderQualityState()
    {
        bool applies = RenderQualityApplies;
        if (!applies) _renderQuality.Close();
        _renderQuality.Opacity = applies ? 1f : DisabledOpacity;
        _renderQualityLabel.Color = applies ? Vector4.One : GrimhollowTheme.TextDisabled;
    }
```

  `GrimhollowRenderQuality` (I7), `Scene3D.CameraCut()`, `Scene3D.LastTemporalDiagnostics` (I1), and on the probe
  branch `ShimmerSession`, `ShimmerView`, `ShimmerConfig`, `ShimmerRig`, `FlickerAccumulator`, `ShimmerBands`,

- Produces: `shimmer --moving [--paths town,forest,meadow] [--moves pan,dolly] [--zooms max,default]
  [--configs fxaa,msaa4,taa-native,taa-quality,taa-balanced,taa-performance,taa-ultraperformance] [--taa-fades 0,1.5,3] [--cost-only]
  [--self-check] [--res WxH] [--frames N] [--warmup N] [--timing-frames N] [out-dir]`, writing `summary.md`,

  `ShimmerHeights.Sample(Vector3, ITileGroundHeight, float)` and `ShimmerDepth.March(FollowCamera3D, ShimmerHeights, int, int, int)`.

Method. Each cell is a path start (the perf verb's town, forest and meadow routes' first tile and yaw and pitch), a
move (a slow pan, an orbit at 0.1 rad/s, one eighteenth of the arrow-key turn `PlayerRig.KeyYawSpeed = 1.8f`, or a
slow dolly in at 0.5 m/s) and a zoom (`PlayerRig.MaxDistance = 22` or `PlayerRig.StartDistance = 12`). Every run
opens a fresh session, applies the choice through the viewer as Settings does (so the wind fade follows), calls
`Scene3D.CameraCut()` before the first frame, and is already moving when the measured window opens. It scores two
things: RAW, the still probe's `FlickerAccumulator` unchanged over the first measured frame's bands, and
COMPENSATED, the same flip rule on each pixel's step against last frame's luma at the reprojected ground point.
Under camera motion the raw count includes content sliding past a pixel, which a softer image scores lower
whether or not it is steadier, so the default rule reads the compensated far band. `--self-check` proves the
compensated metric equals the raw one within 1% on a still camera, where the reprojection is the identity.

```csharp
    /// <summary>Renders frame <paramref name="index"/> at the still view and returns the wait from submit to device
    /// idle, in ms.</summary>
    public double Frame(int index, float frameSeconds) =>
        FrameAt(index, frameSeconds, _view.SubjectTile, _view.Yaw, _view.Pitch, _view.Distance);

    /// <summary>Renders frame <paramref name="index"/> with the orbit camera at one boom, for a moving path. The
    /// boom is written before the viewer's update, as the still probe always did, and again after it, so a
    /// controller that nudged it cannot bend the path.</summary>
    public double FrameAt(int index, float frameSeconds, Vector2 subjectTile, float yaw, float pitch, float distance)
    {
        Camera.Yaw = yaw;
        Camera.Pitch = pitch;
        Camera.Distance = distance;
        Viewer.UpdateLighting(Noon);
        Viewer.Update(_input, frameSeconds);
        Camera.Yaw = yaw;
        Camera.Pitch = pitch;
        Camera.Distance = distance;
        // Update re-aims the boom at the spawn tile when nothing is attached, so the subject goes on after it.
        float groundY = Viewer.Ground.HeightAt(subjectTile.X, subjectTile.Y, 0);
        Camera.Target = TileWorldSpace.ToWorld(subjectTile.X, groundY, subjectTile.Y, Viewer.Document.TileSize);
        // The wind clock is set, not accumulated, so every configuration sees the same instants.
        Scene.EffectTimeSeconds = index * frameSeconds;

        Scene.Begin();
        Viewer.Draw();
        Scene.PrepareFrame();
        using (GpuRecording.Open(Device, _commands, "the shimmer probe's frame list"))
            SceneInternals.Render(Scene, _commands, _width, _height, _framebuffer);
        Device.Submit(_commands);
        long submitted = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
        Device.WaitForIdle();
        return (Stopwatch.GetTimestamp() - submitted) * 1000.0 / Stopwatch.Frequency;
    }
```

`tools/SnapshotTool/ShimmerMetric.cs`, replace lines 27-143 (`ShimmerDepth`) with a heightfield that can be sampled
once and a march over it. The arithmetic is unchanged, so still runs reproduce their old numbers.

```csharp
/// <summary>The ground heightfield the distance march reads, sampled once around a centre on a half metre grid. A
/// moving camera over a fixed subject reuses one sample for every frame.</summary>
sealed class ShimmerHeights
{
    public const float Reach = 220f;
    public const float Cell = 0.5f;

    readonly float[] _heights;
    readonly int _n;
    readonly float _x0, _z0;

    ShimmerHeights(float[] heights, int n, float x0, float z0)
    {
        _heights = heights;
        _n = n;
        _x0 = x0;
        _z0 = z0;
    }

    public static ShimmerHeights Sample(Vector3 centre, ITileGroundHeight ground, float tileSize)
    {
        int n = (int)(2f * Reach / Cell) + 1;
        float x0 = centre.X - Reach, z0 = centre.Z - Reach;
        var heights = new float[n * n];
        for (int iz = 0; iz < n; iz++)
            for (int ix = 0; ix < n; ix++)
            {
                float wx = x0 + (ix * Cell), wz = z0 + (iz * Cell);
                heights[(iz * n) + ix] = ground.HeightAt(TileWorldSpace.TileX(wx, tileSize),
                    TileWorldSpace.TileZ(wz, tileSize), 0);
            }
        return new ShimmerHeights(heights, n, x0, z0);
    }

    public bool TryHeight(float x, float z, out float h)
    {
        float fx = (x - _x0) / Cell, fz = (z - _z0) / Cell;
        h = 0f;
        if (fx < 0f || fz < 0f || fx >= _n - 1 || fz >= _n - 1) return false;
        int ix = (int)fx, iz = (int)fz;
        float tx = fx - ix, tz = fz - iz;
        float a = _heights[(iz * _n) + ix], b = _heights[(iz * _n) + ix + 1];
        float c = _heights[((iz + 1) * _n) + ix], d = _heights[((iz + 1) * _n) + ix + 1];
        h = (a + ((b - a) * tx)) + (((c + ((d - c) * tx)) - (a + ((b - a) * tx))) * tz);
        return true;
    }
}

/// <summary>Per-pixel camera to ground distance for one camera, by marching each pixel's ray over the ground
/// heightfield the viewer's own <see cref="ITileGroundHeight"/> answers. Props, trees and bodies are not in the
/// heightfield, so a pixel covered by a near prop is classed by the ground behind it.</summary>
sealed class ShimmerDepth
{
    const float MaxRay = 400f;

    ShimmerDepth(int width, int height, float[] metres, byte[] band)
    {
        Width = width;
        Height = height;
        Metres = metres;
        Band = band;
    }

    public int Width { get; }
    public int Height { get; }
    public float[] Metres { get; }
    public byte[] Band { get; }

    /// <summary>Marches one ray per <paramref name="block"/> square over a heightfield sampled around the camera's
    /// subject.</summary>
    public static ShimmerDepth March(FollowCamera3D camera, ITileGroundHeight ground, float tileSize,
        int width, int height, int block = 4) =>
        March(camera, ShimmerHeights.Sample(camera.Target, ground, tileSize), width, height, block);

    /// <summary>Marches one ray per <paramref name="block"/> square over an existing heightfield sample.</summary>
    public static ShimmerDepth March(FollowCamera3D camera, ShimmerHeights heights, int width, int height,
        int block = 4)
    {
        // ScreenToRay's own unprojection, done once here so the parallel march never touches the camera's cache.
        Matrix4x4.Invert(camera.ViewProjection, out Matrix4x4 inverse);
        Vector3 origin = camera.RenderOrigin;
        Vector3 eye = camera.Eye;
        int bw = (width + block - 1) / block, bh = (height + block - 1) / block;
        var blockMetres = new float[bw * bh];
        Parallel.For(0, bh, by =>
        {
            for (int bx = 0; bx < bw; bx++)
            {
                float px = MathF.Min(width - 0.5f, (bx * block) + (block * 0.5f));
                float py = MathF.Min(height - 0.5f, (by * block) + (block * 0.5f));
                Vector3 dir = PixelRay(px, py, width, height, inverse, origin, out Vector3 near);
                blockMetres[(by * bw) + bx] = Hit(near, dir, eye, heights);
            }
        });

        var metres = new float[width * height];
        var band = new byte[width * height];
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++)
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++)
            {
                float m = blockMetres[((y / block) * bw) + (x / block)];
                metres[(y * width) + x] = m;
                band[(y * width) + x] = ShimmerBands.Of(m);
            }
        return new ShimmerDepth(width, height, metres, band);
    }

    // Steps grow with range (one percent, at least five centimetres), then a bisection pins the crossing.
    static float Hit(Vector3 start, Vector3 dir, Vector3 eye, ShimmerHeights heights)
    {
        float prev = 0f;
        float t = 0.05f;
        while (t < MaxRay)
        {
            Vector3 p = start + (dir * t);
            if (!heights.TryHeight(p.X, p.Z, out float h)) return float.PositiveInfinity;
            if (p.Y <= h)
            {
                float lo = prev, hi = t;
                for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++)
                {
                    float mid = 0.5f * (lo + hi);
                    Vector3 q = start + (dir * mid);
                    heights.TryHeight(q.X, q.Z, out float hq);
                    if (q.Y <= hq) hi = mid;
                    else lo = mid;
                }
                return Vector3.Distance(eye, start + (dir * hi));
            }
            prev = t;
            t += MathF.Max(0.05f, t * 0.01f);
        }
        return float.PositiveInfinity;
    }

    public static Vector3 Unproject(Vector3 ndc, Matrix4x4 inverse)
    {
        Vector4 p = Vector4.Transform(new Vector4(ndc, 1f), inverse);
        return new Vector3(p.X, p.Y, p.Z) / p.W;
    }

    /// <summary>The world-space ray through the pixel position (<paramref name="px"/>, <paramref name="py"/>), the
    /// unprojection ScreenToRay does, for a caller that already holds the inverse view-projection.</summary>
    /// <param name="near">The ray's start on the near plane, in world space.</param>
    /// <returns>The ray's unit direction.</returns>
    public static Vector3 PixelRay(float px, float py, int width, int height, in Matrix4x4 inverse, Vector3 origin,
        out Vector3 near)
    {
        float ndcX = (px / width * 2f) - 1f, ndcY = 1f - (py / height * 2f);
        near = Unproject(new Vector3(ndcX, ndcY, 0f), inverse) + origin;
        Vector3 far = Unproject(new Vector3(ndcX, ndcY, 1f), inverse) + origin;
        return Vector3.Normalize(far - near);
    }
}
```
